answerNotes.TENOR: Barbershop tenor usually harmonizes above the lead melody.

answerNotes.RESPONSE: A response can repeat or contrast with the opening phrase.
answerNotes.LEADER: A leader initiates the exchange rather than necessarily singing alone throughout.
answerNotes.GOSPEL: Gospel contains different styles and is not defined by one rhythm alone.
answerNotes.AMEN: Amen has religious meaning and can also be part of a musical setting.
answerNotes.CLAP: Clapping supplies percussion without requiring a separate instrument.

answerNotes.ACAPPELLA: A cappella can involve one singer or many, depending on the arrangement.
answerNotes.PITCHPIPE: A pitch pipe can give a starting note without accompanying the entire performance.
answerNotes.BLEND: Blending concerns how voices fit together rather than whether everyone sings one note.
answerNotes.VOCAL: Vocal parts can include melody, harmony, bass, or rhythmic effects.
answerNotes.ARRANGEMENT: An arrangement decides how musical material is shared among the voices.
